title: The Mount of Olives
lead: The ridge just east of Jerusalem, across the Kidron valley. David climbed it weeping when he fled Absalom, Ezekiel saw the glory of the LORD stand on it as it left the city, and Zechariah 14:4 says the LORD's feet will stand on it on the day of the LORD. In the Gospels Jesus teaches, prays and rides down from it, and Acts places his ascension there.

sections.h: From David's flight to the day of the LORD
sections.b: 2 Samuel 15:30 tells how David climbed 'the slope of the Olives,' crying, with his head covered. Ezekiel saw the glory of the LORD leave the Temple and stand on 'the mountain east of the city' (Ezekiel 11:23), and then return from the east (Ezekiel 43:2). Zechariah 14:3-5 has the LORD go out to fight, stand on the Mount of Olives, and split it from east to west, leaving a great valley. This is the only place the Hebrew Bible calls it 'the mountain of the Olives.'

Jesus rides down its slope into Jerusalem (Luke 19:37), sits on it to teach about the end (Matthew 24:3), and goes to it after the last supper (Matthew 26:30). At the ascension two men say he 'will come this same way' (Acts 1:11), and Acts 1:12 places the ascent at the Mount of Olives. Christians and Jews have both linked Zechariah 14:4 to the end; see the cards on the second coming.
